detail.longDescription:
Прикріплено: 1 зображення

thought about replacing obsidian for a great while actually, but just couldn't find *the perfect app* for android and desktop. so last Friday I decided to break down my obsidian usage and cover what I actually need:
- I don't really need links and pictures in my daily diary. It's a diary, not a knowledgebase or personal wiki or whatever! a paper notebook should be enough
- doing something for my uni will make me create a latex file and write down stuff there, which then will be turned into a report that I send as my assignment. no note-taking app needed so far
- if I have a note, todo, or a thought, I could create a file and just write it there in any editor *and* any competent code editor supports markdown syntax highlighting, which is enough for me. sometimes I just create an empty file and write my thought as the filename. I have a shared folder, so synching is solved
- from the "share" menu I can send a link or anything else into Signal "Note To Self" chat. or, again, just put it into the shared folder from previous bullet-point
- "bases" are basically a table with sorting and filtering. if only there was an app designed for that... yeah, LibreOffice Calc with AutoFilter is enough for me, though it's a bit clunky. I get the purpose of bases, but I didn't use it for its fullest

maybe it's not as fancy, but it covers my basic needs and it's as, if not more convenient then a proprietary web based app

I understand the power of a personal wiki, but I just didn't end up doing it

#obsidian #notetaking #productivity
